item.title: Google is helping write AI chatbot safety laws — while pushing for loopholes
item.description: As states push to regulate chatbots, tech companies are trying to write safety rules in ways that exempt some of their key products.

item.title: Army medics being trained to treat wounded military dogs despite supply challenges
item.description: The nature of modern warfare doesn't just mean challenges for treating human casualties. The Army is also training medics to better treat wounded military dogs on the frontlines.

item.title: It's illegal for armed federal officers to be at polls. Lawsuits seek to ensure that
item.description: The latest lawsuit, first reported by NPR, argues the Trump administration's repeated suggestions that federal officers could be at polling sites is a form of illegal voter intimidation.

item.title: The driver who slammed into an LA bus before helicopter crash is charged with murder
item.description: An SUV driver was under the influence of drugs when she swerved into the wrong lane, blew a red light and slammed into a Los Angeles city bus, killing two riders, prosecutors said as they charged her with murder.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Trump withdraws Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, as his nominee to lead ICE
item.description: The White House says it is withdrawing its nomination of Lance Schroyer, a former Oklahoma state trooper, to lead ICE, ensuring that an agency at the forefront of President Trump's domestic agenda will remain without a Senate-confirmed leader for at least a while longer.

item.title: ICE agent appears in Minnesota court to face charges in the shooting of a Venezuelan immigrant
item.description: Christian Castro, a federal immigration officer, made his first court appearance in Minnesota since he was booked Wednesday into a local jail. Castro faces multiple state and federal charges in connection with a shooting during the immigration surge in Minnesota.

item.title: 'American Scoundrel' traces Roy Cohn's playbook from McCarthyism to Trump
item.description: In Kai Bird's biography of Cohn, he looks at how the lawyer taught Trump how to deny, delay, attack, sue and countersue, never admit defeat, side-step paying bills and avoid a paper trail.

item.title: D.C. airspace is complicated. Experts say Trump's arch would add one more risk
item.description: The Trump administration wants to build its 250-foot arch near one of the country's busiest runways. The FAA will determine whether that poses a hazard. But independent experts already have concerns.
